changes.summary: parameter.detach().cpu() -> parameter.detach().cpu().clone(). On CPU the old expression returned the live tensor, so the saved 'best validation' snapshot was rewritten by later epochs and the checkpoint held the final epoch instead. Checked by 'jev-course check' (snapshot_is_independent).

torch.load(..., weights_only=False) -> weights_only=True plus payload shape validation (dict, config dict, state_dict mapping names to tensors, required config keys). Untrusted pickles are refused instead of executed; the on-disk schema is unchanged.

options = list(set) -> sorted(set). Set iteration order depends on PYTHONHASHSEED, so the same seed produced different option orders and labels in different processes. Checked by 'jev-course check' (generation_is_hash_seed_independent).

ECE bins were selected with 'lower <= p < lower + 0.1' against linspace boundaries, which never counted a confidence of exactly 1.0 and depended on float32 equality at the boundaries. Now bin index = floor(p * 10) clamped to [0, 9], so every row belongs to exactly one bin. top1/top3 are unaffected; only the 'ece' value changes.

FrozenTransformerScorer gained an optional third argument, revision (default None), passed straight to AutoModel.from_pretrained. make_system reads config.get('hf_revision') and forwards it to both AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained and the scorer, so a pinned revision is used for the tokenizer and the encoder alike. .get() means a checkpoint written before this key existed still loads and resolves the hub default branch exactly as before; revision=None is the hub default branch.

New --hf-revision argument (default None). When given it is recorded in the checkpoint config as 'hf_revision' so a later load_checkpoint re-resolves the same commit instead of whatever the hub default branch points at; when omitted the config is byte-identical to the pre-change one. No training logic changes.
